subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration: incentives, commit phasing & GPU pool sizing
messages:
From: Janna Rivera <janna.rivera@peregrine.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Alex and I are excited about Redwood's predictable latency profile. We're starting to map out a move from your hosted API to a Dedicated pool for our inference workloads (mainly real-time recommendations and reranking). Before we commit to an internal procurement timeline, we need clarity on the economics if we convert hosted spend into reserved capacity.

Specifically:
- Do you offer an up-front conversion credit to offset hosted usage we already paid for? If so, how does it phase against a committed monthly minimum?
- For a first pass, our estimate is 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed load: 65% short-chat-style requests, 35% long-sequence reranks). Can you advise whether that maps to a single pool or two pools? Any throughput guarantees we should expect per model/slot?
- We also want to understand options for a "bridge" period while we ramp traffic into reserved capacity — e.g., prorated billing or reduced commit for first 3 months.

Attachments: Peregrine_Demo_SLA_Reqs.pdf (SLA items / traffic profile)

Appreciate a short call or a written one-pager we can bring to procurement.

Best,
Janna Rivera
Head of ML Ops, Peregrine Analytics
janna.rivera@peregrine.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Janna Rivera <janna.rivera@peregrine.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Hi Janna — great to hear from you and excited Peregrine is moving forward. High-level answers below; I can follow up with a concrete proposal and numbers.

1) Conversion credit: we offer a time-limited conversion credit that converts a portion of your recent hosted spend into Reserved Commit credit. Typically we structure this as: 40% of eligible hosted spend applied as a one-time credit against the first 6 months of committed fees (i.e., an effective discount that phases out). We can flex that percentage depending on committed term.

2) GPU pool sizing: based on your mix, our recommendation is a single 6-GPU A100-equivalent pool with two VM classes for slot sizing (short-turn and long-turn). That gives you shared KV cache and simpler routing. For throughput SLOs: we guarantee p95 latency for short-turn traffic at the committed throughput lines and hold burst capacity for 2x baseline for 30s. Exact numbers depend on model family and batching config.

3) Bridge period: we commonly offer a 2–3 month bridge where the committed minimum is stepped (e.g., 50% commit Month 1, 75% Month 2, 100% Month 3) while we migrate prefixes and tune caching. During that period the conversion credit is applied preferentially.

I'll assemble a proposed terms workbook (commit vs price vs conversion-credit phasing) and share it later today. Would you be open to a short call on Thursday to review?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Janna Rivera <janna.rivera@peregrine.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moroz <alex.moroz@peregrine.ai>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Ben — thanks, that helps. Two quick clarifications:
- When you say "eligible hosted spend" do you look back 90 days or 12 months? Our spend profile had a burst in Q3.
- For the bridge stepped commit, are consumption above commit billed at hosted rates or at the committed (discounted) rate? We need predictability while we ramp.

If you can put the proposed workbook in a simple line-item table (month, committed GPUs, monthly cost, applied conversion credit, effective per-token cost) that would be perfect.

Janna

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Team — forwarding Peregrine's ask. Key constraints they called out: 6 A100-equivalent target, want 2–3 month bridge, want lookback question answered (Q3 spike).

Action items:
- Ben: please draft the proposed_commit_terms.xlsx with two scenarios: (A) 12-month reserved commit with 40% conversion credit front-loaded over first 6 months; (B) 24-month commit with 55% conversion credit and steeper bridge step (25/50/100). Include per-token effective costs for short-turn vs long-turn workloads.
- Marissa: include an appendix with SLA fallback language — how we fail over to hosted API during partial pool outage and how credits are applied for SLA breaches. Use redwood_sla_fallback-policy.pdf for baseline but highlight any changes for Peregrine.
- Karthik: run a rough throughput estimate mapping their traffic profile to concurrent slot counts and confirm whether a single pool is sufficient vs recommending a split pool. Assume model family similar to Llama-2-13B opt and an average seq-length distribution provided in the PDF.

Timeline: Need a customer-ready packet by Mon 2026-12-06 EOD PST. Ben — can you own collection and final send?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Ack — draft attached. Highlights below (high-level, see workbook):
- Scenario A (12m): commit = 6 GPUs, list price $1.45M/year; conversion credit = 40% of eligible hosted lookback (90-day lookback by default, configurable to 12m if customer provides justification), applied as $X/month over months 1–6 -> effective first-6-month cost drops ~28% on average. Bridge: months 1/2/3 commit steps = 50/75/100%. Consumption above commit billed at hosted rates until commit is reached, then at committed rates thereafter.
- Scenario B (24m): commit = 6 GPUs, list price $1.38M/year (volume rate), conversion credit = 55% of eligible hosted lookback, applied over first 9 months; bridge steps 25/50/100; we include a one-time onboarding credit to cover migration engineering (up to $20k).

Attachments included: proposed_commit_terms.xlsx

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Neha / Ben — I pulled the SLA appendix and made two edits: (1) explicit credit calculation for partial pool loss (pro-rated based on affected GPU-hours), and (2) a temporary routing allowance during Month 1 where we permit up to 15% overflow to hosted with no overage charges while caching warms. See redwood_sla_fallback-policy.pdf (annotated) attached.

Note: legal may push back on open-ended no-overage wording; we should limit to documented traffic patterns in their PDF. I flagged that in the appendix.

Marissa

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Janna Rivera <janna.rivera@peregrine.ai>, Alex Moroz <alex.moroz@peregrine.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated migration — incentives and sizing questions

Hi Janna / Alex — sorry for the runaround, and thanks for your patience. Attached is a customer-ready packet that lays out two commercial paths (12m and 24m) plus the technical appendix. Key points:

- Conversion credit: we use a 90-day lookback by default but will extend to 12 months on documented seasonal spikes; Scenario A applies 40% of eligible hosted spend as credit over first 6 months; Scenario B applies 55% over first 9 months + $20k onboarding credit.
- Bridge months: we recommend the 25/50/100 step for comfort (Scenario B) or 50/75/100 (Scenario A); during the ramp we allow overflow to hosted with predefined tolerances (see appendix).
- GPU pool sizing: Karthik's throughput mapping suggests a single 6-GPU pool will meet their baseline latency SLOs with room for short bursts when combined with the suggested batching profiles. We included an alternative split-pool cost in the workbook in case you want isolation.

Next steps: If this looks good, confirm which scenario (12m vs 24m) and we will route a term sheet + PO path. We can also schedule a 30-minute procurement walkthrough this week if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_commit_terms.xlsx, redwood_sla_fallback-policy.pdf
